facts.statement: The genus name Evgenavis honors the Russian paleontologist Evgeny Kurochkin.
facts.quote: Evgenavis (named after the Russian paleontologist Evgeny Kurochkin)

facts.statement: The type specimen, an isolated tarsometatarsus, was discovered in the Ilek Formation at the Shestakovo locality in Western Siberia.
facts.quote: The type specimen, ZIN PH 1/154, is an isolated tarsometatarsus found in the Ilek Formation (Shestakovo locality), Western Siberia.

facts.statement: Evgenavis existed between 125.77 and 113.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Barremian to Aptian (125.77 to 113.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: Evgenavis is anatomically similar to Confuciusornithiformes, potentially making it the only member of that clade found outside the Jehol Biota.
facts.quote: Evgenavis is anatomically similar to members of the Confuciusornithiformes, which would make it the only member of this clade known outside the Jehol Biota.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analysis resolved Evgenavis as a member of the Enantiornithes.
facts.quote: However, a phylogenetic analysis instead resolved it as a member of the Enantiornithes.

facts.statement: Evgenavis is classified within the parent group Enantiornithes.
Evgenavis is classified under the class Reptilia.
A 2019 study placed Evgenavis as the sister taxon to Longirostravis, which is generally considered a member of the family Longipterygidae.
facts.quote: A cladogram within a 2019 study involving a wide range of theropods included Evgenavis as the sister taxon to Longirostravis, generally regarded as a member of the family Longipterygidae.

rejected.statement: Evgenavis lived during the Barremian to Aptian stages.
rejected.quote: Evgenavis ... lived from the Barremian to the Aptian.
